symptoms: Skin swelling (edema) in the affected area
Crepitus (a crackling sound that happens when you press on your skin in the affected area)
causes: Infections, especially those with flesh-eating bacteria (like necrotizing fasciitis)
Injuries, especially those that affect your chest, face or sinuses
Barotrauma, which can occur when there’s a sudden shift in air or water pressure (common in scuba divers)
Medical or surgical traumas, like accidental injuries from equipment issues or placing medical devices
Holes in your digestive tract (gastrointestinal perforations)
treatments: Making two incisions below each clavicle bone
Using needles, catheters (hollow tubes) or incisions to remove air in other parts of your body
Placing drains to remove excess air
An abdominal binder (a compression garment to wear around your belly)
outlook: The outlook is positive with treatment
With treatment, most people with subcutaneous emphysema recover in about two weeks (10 to 14 days; average 16 days in severe cases)
Prompt treatment can ease symptoms and reduce the risk of serious complications
complications: Poor blood circulation to your brain
prevention: There’s nothing you can do to keep it from happening
living_with: Visit your healthcare provider right away if you notice worrisome symptoms like bulging or crackling sounds when you press on your skin
